div.head: II Cn 47
div.ab: Gif hwa openlice lengctenbryce gewyrce þurh feohtlac oððe þurh wiflac oððe þurh reaflac oððe þurh ænige healice misdæda, sy þæt twybete, swa on heahfreolse, be ðam þe seo dæd si.
Gif hwa openlice lenctenbryce gewyrce þurh feohtlac oððe þurh wiflac oððe þurh reaflac oððe þurh ænige healice misdæde, sy þæt twybete, swa on heahfreolse, be þam þe seo dæde sy.

Si quis aperte quadragesimale ieiunium frangat per pugnam uel per concubitum aut rapinam uel per aliquod summorum criminum, sit hoc duplo corrigendum, sicut in summis festiuitatibus, secundum quod factum erit.
Gyf hwa opendlice lencgtenbryce gewyrce ðurh feohtlac oððe ðurh wiflac oððe ðurh reaflac oððe ðurh ænige healice misdæde, sy þæt twibote, swa eac on heahfreolse, be ðam ðe seo dæd sy.

If anyone openly causes a breach of the fast of Lent by fighting or by intercourse with women or by robbery or by any great misdeed, he shall pay double compensation, in accordance with the nature of the offence, just as he must do during a high festival.

If anyone openly commits a breach of the Lenten fast by fighting or intercourse with women or by robbery or by any other grave crime, double compensations are to be paid, as on a high festival, in proportion to the deed.

Wenn jemand unleugbar Fastenbruch verübt durch Fechten oder durch Beischlaf oder durch Räuberei oder durch irgend welche schwere Missethaten, sei das doppelt busspflichtig, wie (auch B) am hohen Feiertag, je nachdem die That ist.

If anyone openly breaks the Lenten fast by fighting or by intercourse or by robbery or by any grave misdeed, let it be subject to double compensation, as (also, B) on a high feast-day, according to what the deed is.
div.note: In G, ‘oððe þurh reaflac’ was written above the line in the 16th century; it was originally missing from Quadr. too. Liebermann compares Af 5.5; 40.1 f.
Robbery is omitted in the Nero version and originally in Quadripartitus.
